question: What problem did Goldman face in turning the real Butch Cassidy and Sundance into film heroes?
answer: That the real outlaws ran away. Western heroes stand and fight, but Butch and the Sundance Kid fled a posse all the way to South America. Goldman kept the flight and built the film around two charming men whose time was over, which made it fresher than a standard Western and a hit in 1969.
move: A story's awkward truth can be what makes it memorable.
simply: Cowboy heroes are supposed to fight to the end. The real Butch and Sundance ran away. Goldman made the running part of the charm.
why: When a fact doesn't fit the usual story, it's often the most interesting thing about it, in films and in real life.
